text:
You wear God's will as shackles, and law written in sand humbles you; to kiss it you reach shore, obedient sea, driven by surges.


You halt within your pride, humble enough to resist it; your prison amazes you, rich to our harm with our goods.


Who gave pine and beech daring to occupy fishes' dwelling, and linen to obstruct wind?


Surely seeing you captive: greed for pallid gold, God's wrath directed against man.

translation.title: To the Sea
